intro: Searching for an ADHD assessment near you usually means you want clarity about difficulties with focus, organisation or restlessness that are affecting daily life. You may be wondering whether ADHD explains these experiences and where to turn for a proper assessment. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who can discuss your situation and quote you directly.

need_lead: Most people who search for an ADHD assessment near me are looking for a clear, local pathway to understand their symptoms and get an answer.

context_heading: Understanding ADHD assessment and shared care
context: An ADHD assessment involves a detailed history, questionnaires and often input from someone who knew you as a child. It should be carried out by a suitably qualified clinician, such as a psychiatrist registered with the GMC, a practitioner psychologist registered with the HCPC, or a multidisciplinary team following NICE guidance. Clinics carrying out regulated healthcare in England register with the Care Quality Commission; Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own regulators. If you hope your NHS GP will prescribe medication after a private diagnosis, ask in advance whether they will agree to a shared care arrangement, as policies differ between areas and practices. In England, you may also have the option of asking your GP about Right to Choose, which can allow you to be seen by a different provider for NHS-funded care.

When you search for an ADHD assessment near me, it helps to think about what you need from the process: a convenient location, a clinician with experience of adult or child ADHD, and a clear explanation of what the assessment involves. You may also want to know how long the assessment takes, what happens afterwards, and whether the clinician can liaise with your GP. We introduce you to a professional who can answer these questions and provide a quote.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Describe the difficulties you have been experiencing and how long they have been affecting you.
Mention whether you are seeking an assessment for yourself or for someone else, such as your child.
Say whether you have already spoken to your GP or any other professional about your concerns.
Explain whether you are hoping for an assessment through the NHS, privately, or are considering Right to Choose in England.

Include your location and how far you are able to travel for appointments.
questions: What does the assessment process involve and how many appointments will I need?
Are you a psychiatrist registered with the GMC or a practitioner psychologist registered with the HCPC?
Will you provide a written report that I can share with my GP?
Do you follow NICE guidance for ADHD assessments?

faqs.q: Do I need a referral from my GP to get an ADHD assessment?
faqs.a: Not always. Some private clinicians accept self-referrals, while others may ask for a letter from your GP. It is worth asking the professional when you enquire.

faqs.q: What is shared care and why does it matter?
faqs.a: Shared care is an arrangement where your GP prescribes medication recommended by a specialist. Policies differ between practices, so ask in advance whether your GP will agree to this if you receive a private diagnosis.

faqs.q: Can I use Right to Choose for an ADHD assessment?
faqs.a: Right to Choose may apply in England, allowing you to ask your GP to refer you to a different provider for NHS-funded care. Availability can vary, so it is best to discuss this with your GP.

faqs.q: How do I know the clinician is qualified to assess ADHD?
faqs.a: ADHD assessments should be carried out by suitably qualified clinicians, such as a psychiatrist registered with the GMC, a practitioner psychologist registered with the HCPC, or a multidisciplinary team following NICE guidance. You can ask about their qualifications and registration.
